system_description.narrative_title: Fragile multipolar order: bonds, oil and geopolitical escalation
system_description.narrative_summary: The global geopolitical order is an open, tightly coupled system in which surging sovereign yields and a deepening bond rout, energy‑supply shocks from the Middle East and Russia‑Ukraine fighting, and intensifying great‑power rivalry (US‑China, NATO‑Russia) interact to transmit shocks across markets, supply chains and security frameworks. Domestic political shifts and electoral timing—particularly in the United States and Europe—feed back into trade, sanctions, industrial policy and military deployments, while central banks and fiscal moves reshape capital flows and currency dynamics. The system is therefore more fragile and prone to cascading failures across finance, energy and regional security, even as states pursue protective industrial and geopolitical strategies to insulate themselves.
system_description.scope: Nation‑states, alliances and rivalries; international institutions and sanctions regimes; global capital and debt markets; energy and commodity supply chains (oil, diesel, LNG); critical technologies and industrial policy; flows of people, information, materiel and military power.
system_description.super_system: Planetary socio‑economic‑ecological‑technological system (the wider global environment of resources, climate, and enabling technologies within which geopolitics and markets operate).
adjacent_subsystems: Global financial system (sovereign bonds, central banks, credit markets)
Global energy and commodity system (oil, diesel, LNG, refining and shipping)
Regional security architectures (NATO, Middle East security, Indo‑Pacific balances)
Domestic political economies (electoral cycles, industrial policy, social stability)

variables.name: Middle East conflict and Gulf oil disruption
variables.description: A widening Iran‑US proxy and direct confrontation — with Gulf states, Houthi actors and Western forces involved — is reshaping maritime security and intermittently choking crude and refined fuel flows from the Strait of Hormuz and regional terminals.

variables.name: Russia‑Ukraine war and NATO tension
variables.description: Sustained Russian strikes, drone campaigns and hybrid operations against Ukraine — and Moscow’s increasingly aggressive posture toward NATO neighbours — are driving military escalation, wider European defence planning and fears of spillover.

variables.name: U.S.–China strategic rivalry
variables.description: A multifront contest between Washington and Beijing over trade, tariffs, technology controls, critical minerals, military posture around Taiwan and diplomatic leverage is intensifying strategic decoupling while producing episodic cooperation and managed talks.

variables.name: Global bond market rout and rising yields
variables.description: A broad sell‑off in government bonds and a rapid rise in long‑term yields — driven by U.S. macro strength, central‑bank policy uncertainty and inflation risks — is shifting financial conditions, constraining fiscal space and reordering global capital flows.

variables.name: Alliance credibility and realignment under political volatility
variables.description: Growing doubts about U.S. policy predictability and activist domestic politics, alongside European and regional hedging, are prompting allies to reassess burden‑sharing, industrial defence cooperation and contingency planning.
